analysis.title: AI spending as a % of US GDP peaking off in 2026 | MMYT - surprising stock move yesterday
key_insights: GS US economist sees downside risk to 2027 global growth because the AI capex boom has peaked and energy prices remain high.

The growth impulse from the AI boom was set to peak in late 2026 or early 2027, even before concerns about AI investment sustainability intensified in recent weeks. AI investment is still rising rapidly, but its increase as a share of GDP is expected to slow over the next year.
The slowing AI investment share and the fading boost from last year's rise in US depreciation allowances will weigh on capital spending growth, especially in the US.
AI has boosted US consumer spending growth through a wealth effect estimated at 0.4pp (0.25% of GDP) over the past year. That impact is likely to decline over the next year.
MakeMyTrip reported 20% YoY gross booking value growth despite weak air travel growth. GS reads this as the leisure spend budget still growing, with the mode of travel possibly changing.
MakeMyTrip gained share in bus and hotels and held share in air. Management clarified plans for the India listing and fungibility between India shares and US-listed shares.
MakeMyTrip constant-FX revenue rose 20% YoY versus a 16% estimate, on which the stock fell earlier, despite air volumes down 6%. Hotels, bus and share gains supported the result.
MakeMyTrip EBITDA missed the GS estimate by 3% on elevated marketing spend. GS raises revenue estimates by up to 2%, cuts FY27 EBITDA by 5%, and trims TP to US$80 from US$81.
Premium hotel companies (India Hotels, Leela, ITC Hotels) keep reporting strong numbers, while weak air travel data raised worries about mass-market travel and leisure spend.

Paytm 2Q: revenue +28% YoY, EBITDA 10% above GS estimate, further payments share gains and faster Financial Services growth. UPI MDR could add about Rs8-9bn to FY28 EBITDA versus GS's prior 7.5bn. Higher device capex and D&A drive EPS cuts. Buy retained, TP Rs2,010 from Rs2,070.

Tata Consumer 2Q: consolidated revenue +14% YoY, India volumes +11%, EBITDA +17%, growth portfolio +40%. Pricing actions in tea and salt should lift 2H revenue and support management's 50-70bp FY27 EBITDA margin expansion guidance. Buy retained, TP cut to Rs1,325 from Rs1,440 on a lower FMCG target multiple.

Sona Comstar 2Q: revenue +35% and EBITDA +23% YoY, both about 5% ahead of GS estimates, led by EV traction motors, suspension motors and differential assemblies. FY27-29 EPS raised by about 6%/2%/1%. Neutral on valuation, TP Rs860 from Rs855.

ITC Hotels 2Q: RevPAR +21% YoY, revenue +17%, EBITDA +28% and 11% above GS estimate, with roughly 250bp+ margin expansion. RevPAR growth should moderate. FY27-29 EBITDA estimates raised 7-8%. Neutral, TP Rs205 from Rs190.

Urban Company analyst day: management is tracking ahead of its 20%+ core NTV growth trajectory and reiterated Rs10bn consolidated EBITDA by FY31, about 50% above GS's estimate. InstaHelp losses could moderate. Neutral, TP Rs130.

market_movers.rationale: TP trimmed to US$80 from US$81 after FY27 EBITDA was cut 5% on elevated marketing spend. Revenue estimates were raised by up to 2% after a 20% constant-FX revenue beat.
Paytm TP lowered from Rs2,070 on higher device capex and D&A driving EPS cuts, despite revenue +28% YoY and EBITDA 10% above estimate.
Tata Consumer TP cut from Rs1,440 on a lower FMCG target multiple and modest EPS cuts. 2Q revenue +14% YoY and EBITDA +17%.
Sona Comstar TP raised marginally from Rs855 after a 2Q beat of about 5% on revenue and EBITDA. Neutral on valuation.
ITC Hotels TP raised from Rs190 after EBITDA came in 11% above estimate with roughly 250bp+ margin expansion.
Urban Company analyst day takeaways were constructive, with management reiterating Rs10bn consolidated EBITDA by FY31.

sector_views.rationale: GS reads MakeMyTrip's 20% GBV growth and strong premium hotel results as evidence that the leisure spend budget is still growing despite weak air travel data.

Paytm 2Q: revenue +28% YoY reported, EBITDA 10% above GS estimate. UPI MDR could add about Rs8-9bn to FY28 EBITDA versus GS's prior estimate of Rs7.5bn.

Tata Consumer 2Q: consolidated revenue +14% YoY reported, India volumes +11%, EBITDA +17%, growth portfolio +40%. Management guides 50-70bp FY27 EBITDA margin expansion. GS expects a high-teens EBITDA CAGR through FY29.
Sona Comstar 2Q: revenue +35% and EBITDA +23% YoY reported, both about 5% ahead of GS estimates.
